subject: Intermittent packet loss over customer VPN - routing/MSS/SG review
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finserve.com>

Date: 2026-04-05T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent packet loss on our IPsec VPN to Redwood private deployment

Hi Laura / Priyom,

Over the past 36 hours we've been seeing intermittent packet loss and TCP stalls for requests that traverse the VPN to our on-prem Redwood Private cluster. Impact is mostly on larger responses (model outputs > 3kB) — small requests are fine. The problem looks like it correlates with large responses and occasionally recovers for a few minutes.

We suspect either MTU/fragmentation or something odd with our NAT/SGs. Attached is a small pcap captured from our edge inside FinServe when a stalled request occurred (packet_capture.pcap). Can your team review? We're on a tight cadence and this is affecting a production workflow.

Samantha
Network Lead, FinServe

Quick ask: can you confirm whether the FinServe edge is doing MSS clamping for TCP-over-IPsec or if you're relying on PMTUD? Also please include any firewall / NAT gateway config snippets (esp. UDP 4500, ESP, and ICMP types allowed). We'll start by looking at the pcap and the tunnel configuration.

I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth and update as we triage.

Subject: Re: Intermittent packet loss on our IPsec VPN to Redwood private deployment

Laura / Samantha — I pulled the pcap and grabbed a quick look. High level observations (initial):
- I see repeated TCP retransmits following an MSS/fragmentation failure (lots of "Fragmentation needed" ICMPs in capture). That suggests PMTUD is failing.
- The tunnel appears to be using NAT-T (UDP/4500) — watch for path MTU reduction due to UDP encapsulation overhead.
- Important: if intermediate firewalls are blocking ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed), PMTUD won't learn smaller MTU and TCP large packets will be dropped.

Immediate asks to FinServe:
- Confirm whether your edge (or any upstream carrier) is blocking ICMP Type 3 Code 4.
- If you're using an edge NAT, what's the NAT timeout for UDP 4500? Asymmetrical NAT timeouts can drop the ESP flow mid-session.
- Provide the IPsec peer config (transform, MTU/MSS clamping values).

I'll run a couple of packet-level checks from our side (we can also try forcing MSS-clamp on your tunnel and/or lowering MTU on the GW as a mitigation). Marcus — I'll share the pcap and quick tcpdump commands in a follow-up.

-Vivek
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks. Couple of clarifications from our side:
- We are not intentionally blocking ICMP; however, our carrier applies an inline firewall that drops some ICMP. I've opened a ticket with them and attached the carrier trace in the drive link.
- Our edge NAT is a managed gateway. UDP 4500 NAT timeout is 90s by default; we can request an increase.
- Attached the raw pcap from the edge (same as before) and the IPsec peer config exported from the appliance.

Attaching: packet_capture.pcap (original)

We can schedule a quick call if that helps.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finserve.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent packet loss on our IPsec VPN to Redwood private deployment

Folks — I analyzed the provided pcap in more detail and exported a couple of flows. Short summary of findings:
- Several TCP segments from Redwood -> FinServe are marked "Too Big" and are not being retransmitted successfully; I see the server (our host) hit RTO and then recover later. This pattern maps to PMTUD failure (ICMP filtered) or missing MSS clamp.
- The pcap includes multiple fragmented ESP packets — some middleboxes are dropping fragments when ESP is present, which is common when inspection devices see protocol 50 fragments.
- I also observed a handful of asymmetric ACKs — some return traffic takes a different carrier path, which explains intermittent recovery.

Mitigation recommendations (ordered):
1) Enable MSS clamping on the FinServe edge to 1360 — this prevents large TCP segments from requiring fragmentation when encapsulated in UDP/ESP.
2) Confirm with carrier to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) across the path; this restores PMTUD if MSS clamping can't be applied immediately.
3) Increase NAT keepalive/UDP 4500 timeout to >= 300s to avoid mid-session NAT expiry.
4) As a short-term test, we can lower the MTU on the Redwood-backed gateway interface to 1400 and monitor. This is low-risk and reversible.

I've uploaded an annotated pcap and quick commands to our shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExample and created INF-2142 in Jira for the follow-up remediation.

I'll hold off on changes on our side until FinServe confirms MSS clamp or carrier changes. Happy to do a joint maintenance window.

-Marcus
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-deployment-diagram.png

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps so FinServe and internal teams are aligned: 
- Action items for FinServe: (1) Request carrier to allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4; (2) Enable MSS clamping on edge (1360) and/or increase UDP 4500 NAT timeout to 300s.
- Action items for Redwood: (1) Prepare a maintenance window to lower MTU on our gateway to 1400 (non-disruptive test) if FinServe cannot enable MSS clamp quickly; (2) Monitor INF-2142 and provide post-change pcap analysis.

I'll schedule a 30-minute troubleshooting window tomorrow at 09:00 PT for hands-on testing if that works for your team, Samantha. Priyom will coordinate scheduling.
